questions.question: Pre-trip inspections:

options.text: Should never be done the same way twice.
Should always be done in the same order.
Do not need to be done if you know the vehicle well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should always be done in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do vehicle inspections in the same order every time. This helps you learn the steps and makes it less likely you will forget to check something.

questions.question: When starting from a stop:

options.text: A vehicle should shift to the right.
A vehicle should be put into third gear.
A vehicle should not roll back.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle should not roll back.
questions.explanation: Keep your vehicle from rolling backward when you start from a complete stop. This prevents hitting things behind you.

questions.question: Hazardous materials placards are usually shaped like:

options.text: Circles.
Triangles.
Diamonds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamonds.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: While driving:

options.text: You do not need to tell others what you plan to do.
You should only use turn signals if a vehicle is next to you.
You should not use a turn signal if your lane change is obvious.
You should always use turn signals to tell others your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always use turn signals to tell others your plans.
questions.explanation: Always use proper signals to let other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.question: When driving a tractor-trailer with ABS, you should:

options.text: Stop harder than usual.
Use extra braking force to activate the ABS.
Brake as you normally would.
Brake using less pressure than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake as you normally would.
questions.explanation: When driving a tractor-trailer with an anti-lock braking system (ABS), brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while carrying liquids, one safe option is to:

options.text: Turn while braking.
Apply the emergency brake.
Apply light brake pressure.
Use the stab braking method.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the stab braking method.
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly to avoid an accident while carrying liquids, the stab braking method is a good choice. Do not try to steer quickly while braking—this may tip your vehicle over, especially if it has a high center of gravity.

questions.question: When drivers turn, they usually:

options.text: Look in the direction of the turn.
Look in the opposite direction of the turn.
Look behind their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, drivers look in the direction they are turning. If a driver does not signal before turning or changing lanes, their body movements may show they plan to turn.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is recommended.
Can cause mechanical damage.
Is required on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause mechanical damage.
questions.explanation: Always speed up slowly and smoothly so your vehicle does not jerk. Rough acceleration can damage the engine and other parts.

questions.question: Who must identify the hazard class of a hazardous material?

options.text: The shipper
A contractor
The driver
Everyone

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for determining the product's ID number, proper shipping name, hazard class, and packing group. They also decide what packaging, labels, markings, and placards to use.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve will pop out when:

options.text: Air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
The trailer jackknifes.
Wheels grip the road again after a skid.
Air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out if air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: The heavier a vehicle is:

options.text: The less important brakes become.
The harder the brakes must work.
The quieter the brakes will sound.

questions.correctAnswerText: The harder the brakes must work.
questions.explanation: Heavy vehicles need stronger braking power to stop completely.

questions.question: A lightly-loaded combination vehicle stops more slowly than a fully-loaded vehicle because:

options.text: Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes have high traction.
Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes have low traction.
Brakes only work when a trailer reaches a minimum weight.
Suspension springs only work when a trailer reaches a minimum weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes have low traction.
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle stops more slowly than a fully-loaded vehicle. Light trailers have less traction with their suspension springs and brakes than heavier, fully-loaded vehicles.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, the driver should:

options.text: Ignore the report and find any issues themselves.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Read the report.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and use only the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the report.
questions.explanation: Start your vehicle inspection by reading the last inspection report. The carrier should have fixed any problems listed on it.

questions.question: When loading a tank divided by bulkheads with liquid cargo, most of the weight should go:

options.text: In the top of the tank.
In the middle of the tank.
In the rear of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle of the tank.
questions.explanation: Do not place too much weight on the front or rear of a divided tank. Keep the weight balanced in the middle.

questions.question: Placards must be used:

options.text: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
If there is empty space in the truck.
If hazardous materials in the truck exceed 200 pounds.
If hazardous materials create an inhalation hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show the type of material and warn others of the hazard.

questions.question: People working on a disabled vehicle:

options.text: Are probably aware of the roadway.
May be focused on repairs and not notice nearby traffic.
Are not subject to traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on repairs and not notice nearby traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive carefully near people working on a disabled vehicle. They may be concentrating on their repair and not watching traffic.

questions.question: If hazardous cargo is leaking and the driver has no phone, they should:

options.text: Drive to find a phone to alert emergency personnel.
Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility.
Send someone else to get help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Send someone else to get help.
questions.explanation: If hazardous cargo leaks, do not drive the vehicle more than needed. Driving spreads contamination over a larger area. Instead, park safely, stay with the vehicle, and send someone to call emergency personnel.

questions.question: If cargo is leaking, you should:

options.text: Touch the material to identify the cargo.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify the cargo.
Assume all cargo is leaking.
Spray leaking containers with water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify the cargo.
questions.explanation: If you find a leak in hazardous cargo, identify the material using shipping papers and labels. Do not touch the leaking material.

questions.question: While driving:

options.text: Sending a text is not allowed, but reading one is.
Sending a text is allowed, but reading one is not.
Sending and reading texts are both not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sending and reading texts are both not allowed.
questions.explanation: You cannot text while driving a commercial motor vehicle. This includes typing text messages or reading them.

questions.question: During pre-trip inspections:

options.text: Use the same process each time.
Check different items each time.
It is okay to check items in a different order each time.
You do not need to inspect every item each time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the same process each time.
questions.explanation: Always do pre-trip inspections the same way. This helps you remember to check all important items.
